mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month acceleration in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 3% annualized coincides with higher corporate earnings expectations, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If 60-day forward returns are not positive in at least 70% of triggered episodes, or if IC drops below 0.05 for 3 consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the unemployment rate above 6.5% signals deteriorating consumer demand, reducing earnings growth and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 60% of triggered episodes, or if IC falls below 0.02 for any 12-month window.

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 1% annualized, coinciding with rising unemployment (UNRATE > 6.5%), predicts negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to recessionary signals.
failure_condition: If 20-day forward returns are not negative in at least 65% of triggered episodes, or if IC drops below 0.01 for any 18-month window.
